{"timeline":[{"headline":"Film Announcement","text":"Transformers: Age of Extinction was officially announced as the fourth installment in the Transformers film series, directed by Michael Bay.","date":"2012"},{"headline":"Casting Announcement","text":"Mark Wahlberg was announced as the lead actor for Transformers: Age of Extinction, replacing the original human cast from the previous films.","date":"2012-11"},{"headline":"Filming Begins","text":"Principal photography for Transformers: Age of Extinction began in various locations, including the United States and China.","date":"2013-05"},{"headline":"Filming Concludes","text":"Filming for Transformers: Age of Extinction wrapped up after several months of production.","date":"2013-10"},{"headline":"Film Release","text":"Transformers: Age of Extinction was released in theaters on June 27, 2014, becoming the fourth installment in the Transformers film series.","date":"2014-06-27"},{"headline":"Box Office Success","text":"Transformers: Age of Extinction grossed over $1.1 billion worldwide, making it one of the highest-grossing films of 2014.","date":"2014"}]}

{"timeline":[{"headline":"Ancient Greek Practice","text":"Intercrural sex was a common practice in ancient Greek society prior to the early centuries AD. It was frequently discussed by writers and portrayed in artwork such as vases.","date":"-0001"},{"headline":"Subject to Sodomy Laws","text":"Intercrural sex later became subject to sodomy laws and became increasingly seen as contemptible.","date":"0000"},{"headline":"17th Century Cultural Prominence","text":"In the 17th century, intercrural sex was featured in several works of literature and took cultural prominence, being seen as a part of male-on-male sexual habits.","date":"1600"},{"headline":"Trial of Mervyn Tuchet","text":"The trial and execution of Mervyn Tuchet, 2nd Earl of Castlehaven, in 1631 brought attention to intercrural sex as part of male-on-male sexual habits.","date":"1631"}]}

{"timeline":[{"headline":"Origins of Tennis","text":"The origins of tennis can be traced back to 12th century France, where a game called 'jeu de paume' was played with the hand. By the 16th century, rackets were introduced, and the game began to be called 'tennis.'","date":"-1100"},{"headline":"First Tennis Tournament","text":"The first known tennis tournament was held in 1877 at the All England Club in Wimbledon, London. This event marked the beginning of the Wimbledon Championships, the oldest tennis tournament in the world.","date":"1877"},{"headline":"Introduction of Lawn Tennis","text":"In 1873, Major Walter Clopton Wingfield introduced a game called 'Sphairistikè' (Greek for 'playing ball') which was played on an hourglass-shaped court. This game evolved into what is now known as lawn tennis.","date":"1873"},{"headline":"Establishment of the International Lawn Tennis Federation","text":"The International Lawn Tennis Federation (ILTF) was founded in 1913 to oversee the rules and regulations of tennis worldwide. It later became the International Tennis Federation (ITF).","date":"1913"},{"headline":"Tennis Becomes an Olympic Sport","text":"Tennis was included in the first modern Olympic Games in Athens in 1896. However, it was removed after the 1924 Games and was reintroduced as a full medal sport in 1988 at the Seoul Olympics.","date":"1988"},{"headline":"Open Era Begins","text":"The Open Era began in 1968 when Grand Slam tournaments agreed to allow professional players to compete with amateurs. This marked a significant change in the sport, leading to increased popularity and commercial success.","date":"1968"},{"headline":"Introduction of the ATP and WTA Tours","text":"The Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) was formed in 1972 to protect the interests of male professional tennis players. The Women's Tennis Association (WTA) was founded in 1973 for female players.","date":"1972"},{"headline":"Introduction of the Tie-Break","text":"The tie-break was introduced in 1970 to decide sets that reach a 6-6 score, adding a new strategic element to the game.","date":"1970"},{"headline":"Adoption of Electronic Line Calling","text":"In 2006, the Hawk-Eye electronic line calling system was introduced at professional tournaments, allowing players to challenge line calls and improving the accuracy of officiating.","date":"2006"}]}
